## Known biases

The rule was fitted to NFIP claims 2017-2022 in the 100 highest-claim 75 km cells of the conterminous US (about 81% of pluvial claims), which are in the Northeast and Gulf regions; the shares 81.1/12.9/6.0 describe those claims, not New York City alone. AORC rainfall at the claim location is the only judge of a correct date, so claims for non-rain causes (tidal, river) are also dropped or moved.

<details><summary>Passage: rule text</summary>

<pre>&quot;3.1.1 Temporal Uncertainty Correction. The dateOfLoss field in the NFIP claims data is known to be noisy where reported dates of loss often fail to align with precipitation events in the historical precipitation records. ... To mitigate this noise, we apply the following correction to the dateOfLoss field d: (1) Compute the daily maximum hourly accumulated precipitation from NOAA AORC [21] for day d at the location of the claim. (2) If the daily maximum hourly accumulated precipitation on day d exceeds 10 mm, accept dateOfLoss as reported. (3) Otherwise, search the window d&#x27; in {d - 3, ..., d + 3} and select the day with the largest daily maximum hourly precipitation. If this maximum exceeds 10 mm, update dateOfLoss to d&#x27;. (4) If no day&#x27;s daily maximum hourly precipitation in the window exceeds 10 mm, discard the claim as erroneous.&quot;</pre>

</details>
